items.stem: What is the core idea of the red-green-refactor cycle in TDD?

options.text: Write a failing test, make it pass simply, then improve the design while keeping tests green
options.rationale: Correct: that is the three-step TDD loop.

options.text: Write all code first, then add tests at the end

options.rationale: Refactoring comes after a passing test.

options.text: Delete tests once the code works
options.rationale: Tests are kept as a safety net.

items.explanation: Correct: that is the three-step TDD loop.

items.stem: How does trunk-based development with small batches shorten feedback loops?

options.text: Frequent small integrations surface conflicts and defects quickly rather than at a late merge
options.rationale: Correct: small, frequent merges reduce integration risk.

options.text: It removes the need for a CI pipeline
options.rationale: CI is essential to trunk-based development.

options.text: It eliminates the need for tests

options.text: The build should run automatically on every push
options.rationale: Correct: automated builds catch breakage early.

options.text: A broken main build should be fixed before starting new work
options.rationale: Correct: keeping the build green protects the team.
